title: Leaf count after path deletion
statement:
Let $s$ be a protocol with a subprotocol path into $r$, let $P$ be a family of protocols indexed by bits, and let $b$ be a bit such that $P(b)=r$. Let $N$ be a constructor on protocol families, and let $Q$ assign a protocol family to each protocol, with $Q(q_c)(b)=q_c$ and $Q(q_c)(
eg b)=P(
eg b)$ for every $q_c$. Suppose the result $q$ of the following case distinction is specified by $q=P(
eg b)$ if deleting the path from $r$ to $s$ returns nothing, and by $q=N(Q(q_c))$ if deletion returns $q_c$. Assume $N$ has leaf count equal to the sum of the leaf counts of its two children, and that whenever deletion returns some protocol $q'$, its leaf count is $\ell(r)-\ell(s)$. Then $\ell(q)=\ell(N(P))-\ell(s)$, where subtraction is truncated subtraction on the natural numbers.
hypotheses_covered: The deletion case distinction yields $q$ as stated
For every $q'$, if deletion returns $q'$, then $\ell(q')=\ell(r)-\ell(s)$
replaced:
Let $s$ be a subprotocol of $r$ via a subprotocol path $h_s$, let $P$ be a family of
children with $P(b) = r$, and let $N$ be a node constructor whose leaf count is the sum of
its two children's leaf counts. Let $Q$ be a rebuilding map with $Q(q_c)(b) = q_c$ and
$Q(q_c)(\neg b) = P(\neg b)$, and suppose $q$ is the result of deleting along the path
inside branch $b$: $q = P(\neg b)$ if the deletion of $h_s$ returns nothing, and
$q = N(Q(q_c))$ if it returns $q_c$. Assume (inductively) that whenever the deletion of
$h_s$ returns some $q'$ one has $\ell(q') = \ell(r) - \ell(s)$. Then
\[
  \ell(q) = \ell(N(P)) - \ell(s) .
\]
